name: Hypoplasia of the Mitral Valve Annulus

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of reduced mitral valve annulus diameter relative to body surface area
Presence of mitral valve dysfunction such as mitral regurgitation or stenosis secondary to annular hypoplasia
Exclusion of other structural cardiac defects that could explain mitral valve abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of mitral valve annulus hypoplasia with associated mitral valve dysfunction and exclusion of other cardiac anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory markers identified
imaging: Echocardiography showing reduced mitral valve annulus diameter and mitral valve dysfunction
Cardiac MRI may demonstrate annular hypoplasia and associated structural abnormalities
Chest X-ray showing left atrial enlargement and pulmonary congestion in advanced cases
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be sporadic or part of complex congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram may show left atrial enlargement or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or enlarged mitral annulus size
Leaflet prolapse rather than annular hypoplasia
Thickened mitral leaflets and commissural fusion
Annulus size typically normal or dilated
Other structural abnormalities such as parachute mitral valve or cleft mitral valve

redFlags: Severe mitral regurgitation causing heart failure symptoms in infancy
Progressive left atrial enlargement with risk of arrhythmias
Signs of pulmonary hypertension secondary to mitral valve dysfunction
